# Propose a change to the architecture record

Everything under `architecture/` is generated from Ergane and overwritten
on the next publish, so an edit made here is an edit that will disappear
without anybody noticing. Changes are proposed instead as **change-sets**:
semantic operations validated against the type definitions before they
are applied, applied all-or-nothing, and recorded against whoever made
them.

## When to raise one

Raise a change-set when the record is wrong or incomplete, not when the
code is. A service that exists in code and not in the model is usually a
change-set; a service that exists in the model and not in code is usually
a drift finding. If you cannot tell which, report it and say so.

## The shape of a change-set

```json
{
  "title": "Settlement workers are their own service",
  "rationale": "Extracted from the ledger service in the queue rework",
  "operations": [
    { "op": "createEntity", "typeKey": "<the type's key from graph.json>",
      "name": "Settlement workers" },
    { "op": "set", "entityId": 731, "sectionKey": "characteristics",
      "fieldKey": "risk", "value": 7 },
    { "op": "link", "sourceEntityId": 731, "targetEntityId": "$new[0]",
      "kind": "ref" }
  ]
}
```

Read `architecture/definitions/<type>.codl-def.json` for the section and
field keys before you write one — the field types, legal values and legal
links are all declared there, and a change-set that disagrees with the
definition is refused rather than half-applied.

`$new[i]` names the i-th `createEntity` in the same change-set, counting
from 0, and that create must come earlier in the `operations` array.
It is accepted wherever an operation takes an entity id:
`entityId`, `sourceEntityId` and `targetEntityId`. So the `link` above,
from an existing entity to the one just created, is legal in one
change-set.

It is never inside a `$ref` value. A reference stored in a field
(`{"$ref": {"entityId": 812}}` in a `set`) needs a real id: create the
entity in one change-set, then set the reference in a second one, using
the id the first returned.

A `link` needs a `kind`: a short label you choose for the relationship
(the service requires one and does not restrict it). The graph's own
field references use `ref`.

## How to submit it

Validate, then apply, through the BTABoK MCP server at
`https://mcp.iasaglobal.org`. It needs an API key, sent as
`Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key: <key>`; setup for each agent
is at https://education.iasaglobal.org/mcp. The tools are
`loom_validate_change_set` and `loom_apply_change_set` (they keep the
`loom_` prefix; the product is Ergane). Validation writes nothing and says
what is wrong; run it first, every time.

If you have no route to that server, write the change-set into the pull
request description under a heading saying what it is, and say plainly
that the architecture record has not been updated. A change nobody records
is a change the next agent will contradict.
